mainTopic: Closing the discussion of a נזיר's lashes and grape parts; a new משנה on the thirty-day נזירות and shaving; and whether hair grows from the root or the tip
overview: The גמרא first asks why רב פפא challenged אביי with a version of a ברייתא that does not actually say 'five.' רב פפא explains that he was testing whether אביי's view was a received tradition, and it turned out that it was. Next, רב יוסף notes that the standard תרגום of 'מחרצנים ועד זג' follows רבי יוסי. A new משנה then teaches that an unspecified נזירות lasts thirty days. Shaving cancels thirty days, even when bandits do it, and a נזיר who removes hair in any way is liable. The גמרא asks whether hair grows from the bottom or from the top. This matters for a נזיר whose hair was only partly shaved. Proofs from live lice, dead lice and braided hair are each pushed off. The גמרא then brings proofs from dyed sheep wool and old men's dyed beards, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why did רב פפא object using five?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב פפא challenged אביי with a ברייתא counting five sets of lashes, when the real ברייתא does not say five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged אביי by quoting a teaching that counts five. But the teaching does not actually say five. So why did he challenge him that way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by רב פפא's earlier challenge to אביי. It is setting up רב פפא's own explanation, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב פפא challenged אביי from a ברייתא as if it listed five sets of lashes. Since the real ברייתא does not list five, the challenge seems to rest on a wrong quote. The גמרא wants to know what he was doing.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him; he raised an objection against him

phrases.english: He objected to him with five,
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא challenging אביי, using a ברייתא as if it counted five sets of lashes.

phrases.english: but since five is not taught,
what is the reason he objected to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up from the earlier discussion between רב פפא and אביי (before this section).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב פפא based his challenge on a version of the ברייתא that does not read 'five'.

steps.title: רב פפא was testing whether אביי had a tradition
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that he thought אביי's view was only his own reasoning and would be dropped under pressure. He did not know it was a received tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: I thought אביי did not have this from a tradition, so he would take it back. I did not know that it was a tradition he had received, which is why he did not take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question himself. He explains that his challenge was a test to see whether אביי would back down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a view is only someone's own reasoning, a strong source against it should make him retract. אביי held firm, which showed that his view came from a received tradition. So the challenge failed, and רב פפא admits that he had misjudged.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a received tradition, passed down from teachers
In his hand; he has it
He retracts; he takes back his view

steps.whatToRemember: A view that comes from a received tradition (גמרא) is not dropped just because a challenge is raised against it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא סְבַרִי לָאו גְּמָרָא הִיא בִּידֵיהּ,
phrases.english: I thought it was not a tradition in his hand,
phrases.notes: 'His' means אביי's. Here גמרא means a teaching passed down from his teachers.

phrases.english: and so he would retract.
And I did not know that it was a tradition in his hand,
and so he did not retract.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The challenge was a test. רב פפא thought אביי's view was his own reasoning and that he would retract, but it was a received tradition, so he held firm.

steps.title: The תרגום of 'from seeds to skins' follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the earlier משנה, רב יוסף says the Aramaic translation of 'מחרצנים ועד זג' as 'מפורצנין ועד עיצורין' follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says, and so on. רב יוסף said: Whose view does our translation 'מפורצנין ועד עיצורין' follow? It follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the earlier משנה about the grape parts a נזיר may not eat. רב יוסף points out which opinion the standard תרגום matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה brought two views about which part of the grape is called חרצן and which is called זג. The תרגום translates the פסוק as going 'from the seeds to the skins'. That makes חרצן the seed and זג the skin, which is the view of רבי יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says, etc.
Rav Yosef said:
In accordance with whom do we translate
"from the seeds to the skins"?
phrases.notes: This is the Aramaic translation of 'מחרצנים ועד זג', במדבר 6:4.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the earlier משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תרגום's reading, that חרצנים are seeds and זג is the skin, matches רבי יוסי.

steps.title: משנה: unspecified נזירות is thirty days, and shaving cancels thirty days
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a נזירות with no length stated lasts thirty days. If the נזיר shaved, or bandits shaved him, he loses thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: An unspecified נזירות lasts thirty days. If he shaved, or bandits shaved him, this cancels thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the default length of נזירות and the penalty for shaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone takes on נזירות without saying how long, it lasts thirty days. Shaving cancels thirty days of counting, so he must count them again. This applies even when bandits shaved him against his will.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזירות with no length stated

steps.confusionAlert: Even when bandits shave him by force, he still loses thirty days. The shaving cancels the days even though it was not his fault.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A naziriteship of unspecified length is thirty days.
If he shaved, or bandits shaved him,
it cancels thirty days.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified נזירות lasts thirty days. Shaving, even when bandits do it, cancels thirty days.

steps.title: משנה: any way of removing hair makes the נזיר liable
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who removes hair is liable whether he used scissors or a razor, or pulled out even a tiny amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נזיר who shaved, whether with scissors or with a razor, or who pulled out any amount at all, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It explains which ways of removing hair make a נזיר liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is not limited to shaving with a razor. Cutting with scissors also counts, and so does pulling out even the smallest amount of hair.
steps.whatToRemember: An unspecified נזירות is thirty days. Shaving cancels thirty days, even if bandits did it. Any removal of hair, by any method, makes the נזיר liable.

phrases.aramaic: נָזִיר שֶׁגִּילַּח בֵּין בְּזוּג בֵּין בְּתַעַר,
phrases.english: A nazirite who shaved, whether with scissors or with a razor,
or who pulled out any amount, is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר שֶׁגִּילַּח בֵּין בְּזוּג בֵּין בְּתַעַר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing hair in any way (scissors, razor, or pulling out any amount) makes the נזיר liable.

steps.title: Does hair grow from the bottom or from the top?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a question: does hair grow from the root at the bottom, or from the tip at the top?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Does this hair grow from below or from above?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion with a factual question about how hair grows. It is setting up a question about why the answer matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is which part of a hair is the new growth: the part near the root, or the part at the tip. The גמרא will now explain how this connects to the laws of a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַזְיָא מִלְּתַחַת רָבֵי אוֹ מִלְּעֵיל?
phrases.english: Does this hair grow from below or from above?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the new משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hair grows from the root end or from the tip end.

steps.title: Why it matters: a נזיר whose hair was not fully shaved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question matters for a נזיר whom bandits shaved but left enough hair to bend its tip back to its root.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? It matters for a נזיר whom bandits shaved, but they left enough hair on him to bend its tip down to its root.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the hair question matters and answers with a specific case. This links the question back to the משנה's case of bandits shaving a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said shaving cancels thirty days. Here the bandits did not shave him completely; some hair remained, long enough to fold its tip back to its root. Whether hair grows from below or from above affects how we look at this leftover hair.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
To bend its tip down to its root

steps.whyThisMatters: This case is the measuring stick for deciding whether a partly shaved נזיר has kept enough hair, and it ties the growth question directly to the משנה's rule.

phrases.english: For what is there a practical difference?
For a nazirite whom bandits shaved

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁיְּירוּ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לָכוֹף רֹאשׁוֹ לְעִיקָּרוֹ.
phrases.english: and they left on him enough to bend its tip to its root.
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the hair: what is left is long enough to fold the tip of each hair back down to where it starts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the question in step 6 matters.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference arises for a נזיר whom bandits shaved but left enough hair to bend its tip to its root.

steps.title: The two sides: is the sanctified hair gone or still there?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out what each side of the question means for the נזיר who was shaved by bandits but still has a little hair left.
steps.simpleTranslation: If hair grows from the bottom, the bandits removed the hair of his נזירות. If hair grows from the top, the hair he sanctified is still on his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step by showing the practical result of each side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If new hair pushes up from the root, the old sanctified hair sat at the tip, and the bandits cut it off. So his נזירות hair is gone. If new hair is added at the tip, the old sanctified hair is the part still near the scalp, so it is still there.

keyTerms.meaning: The נזיר's vow; here it means the hair that grew during the vow

steps.confusionAlert: Picture it carefully. If hair grows from the root, the OLDEST hair ends up at the far tip, which is exactly the part the bandits cut off.

phrases.english: If you say it grows from below,
then he has taken off the hair of the נזירות.
phrases.notes: The old, sanctified hair got pushed up to the end, and that is the part the bandits cut.

phrases.english: But if you say it grows from above,
then what he sanctified is still standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation from step 7 of why the question about hair growth matters.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Growth from the root means the sanctified hair was removed. Growth from the tip means the sanctified hair is still there.

steps.title: Proof from a live louse sitting at the root
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove that hair grows from the tip, because a live louse is always found near the root.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a live louse is found at the root of the hair. If hair grew from the bottom, the louse should be carried up to the end of the hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an observation from nature to try to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a louse holding onto a hair moves along with it. If hair grew from the root, the louse would slowly be lifted toward the tip. Since live lice sit at the root, it seems hair grows from the top.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind, if you were to think

phrases.english: Come and hear from this live louse
which stays at the root of the hair.
And if you think it grows from below,
it should be found at the tip of the hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question from step 6 using an observation about lice.
steps.raayaObject: That hair grows from the tip
steps.raayaSupportSource: Live lice are found at the root of the hair

steps.title: A live louse crawls back down
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Hair may really grow from the root, and the live louse just keeps crawling down toward the scalp.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it grows from below. Because the louse is alive, it keeps crawling down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the louse proof with another way to explain why the louse is at the root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The louse being at the root does not prove anything about how hair grows. A live louse can move by itself, so even if the hair carries it up, it walks back down.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (used to keep the original option)

phrases.english: Really, it grows from below,
and because it is alive, the louse keeps going down.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the live-louse proof only; the question stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A live louse moves by itself, so where it sits says nothing about how hair grows.

steps.title: Proof from a dead louse at the tip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the opposite proof: a dead louse is found at the tip, which suggests hair grows from the root.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a dead louse is found at the tip of the hair. If hair grew from the top, the dead louse should stay at the root.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second observation, this time pointing to the other side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead louse cannot move, so it should show how the hair really grows. Since it ends up at the tip, the hair must have pushed it up from below. That means hair grows from the root.

phrases.english: Come and hear: a dead louse
is at the tip of the hair.
And if you think it grows from above,
it should be found at the root of the hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, a new proof is offered for the opposite side.
steps.raayaObject: That hair grows from the root
steps.raayaSupportSource: Dead lice are found at the tip of the hair

steps.title: A dead louse gets stuck and carried up
steps.stepSummary: This proof is also pushed off. Hair may grow from the top, and the dead louse just gets tangled and pulled along.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too: because it has no strength, it gets tangled up and goes along.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the dead-louse proof with another explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead louse has no strength to hold its place, so it gets caught in the hair and moved around. Where it ends up does not prove which way the hair grows.

keyTerms.meaning: There too, the same kind of answer works
It gets tangled or caught up

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם נָמֵי, מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵית בַּהּ חֵילָא
phrases.english: There too, since it has no strength,
it gets tangled and goes along.
phrases.notes: He means the dead louse gets caught in the hair and drifts along with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵית בַּהּ חֵילָא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A dead louse gets tangled and carried along, so where it lands proves nothing.

steps.title: Proof from braided long hair going loose at the bottom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a third proof: the long braided hair of non-Jews gets loose near the scalp, which suggests new hair grows from below.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the long hair of the כושיים: after they braid it, it becomes loose underneath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third observation, again pointing toward hair growing from the root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The braid stays tight at the ends, but the part near the head becomes loose. That makes it look like new, unbraided hair is coming out from the root.

keyTerms.meaning: Long grown-out hair, worn as a non-Jewish style
They grow it out (here, they braid it)

phrases.english: Come and hear from the long hair of the Cushites,
that after they braid it,
it becomes loose from below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two failed lice proofs, a new proof from braided hair is offered.
steps.raayaObject: That hair grows from the root
steps.raayaSupportSource: Braided long hair loosens near the scalp

steps.title: The braid loosens from being slept on
steps.stepSummary: The third proof is pushed off. The braid loosens near the bottom because it gets crushed when the person lies on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too: since it gets crumpled from lying down, it becomes loose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the braided-hair proof. It then goes on to try further proofs in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The looseness can come from pressure, not from new growth. When a person lies on the braid it gets squashed and loosened, so it proves nothing about which way hair grows.
steps.whatToRemember: The first three proofs (live louse, dead louse, braided hair) all fail, because each one has another explanation. The גמרא then tries new proofs from dyed sheep wool and dyed beards (steps 15–16).

phrases.english: There too, since it gets crumpled
from lying down, it becomes loose.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the braided-hair proof only; further proofs follow in steps 15–16.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The looseness comes from being lain on, not from new hair growing at the root.

steps.title: Proof from dyed sheep wool
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a fourth proof: when sheep are marked with dye, the dyed wool becomes loose at the bottom near the skin. This suggests new wool grows from the root. It notes that this practice also appears in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof from the dye put on sheep. The dyed wool becomes loose from underneath. And this is taught in a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another proof that hair grows from the root, using the dye people put on sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When wool is dyed, the color stays on the old part of the wool. If the dyed part pulls away near the skin, then new, undyed wool must be pushing out from the bottom. The word וְתַנְיָא shows this is a real practice mentioned in a ברייתא, not just a story someone made up.

keyTerms.meaning: Red dye used to mark sheep

phrases.english: Come and hear from the dye used on sheep,
for the wool becomes loose from underneath,
and it was taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the braid proof was pushed off in step 14, the גמרא brings a new, independent proof for the same side of the question from step 6: hair grows from the root.
steps.raayaObject: Hair grows from the root, at the bottom.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The everyday observation that dyed wool on sheep loosens near the skin, backed by a ברייתא that mentions sheep-dyeing.

steps.title: Proof from old men who dye their beards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another proof: when old men dye their beards, the beards turn white again. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: when old men dye their beards, they become white again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more proof that hair grows from the root, this time from old men who dye their white beards. The sentence is not finished yet. It continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An old man dyes his white beard dark, but after a while white shows up again. That white must be new hair coming out, which points the same way as the sheep proof: new hair grows from below.

phrases.english: And furthermore: when they dye,
old men's beards turn white
phrases.notes: Literally "when old men dye their beards, white..." The sentence keeps going on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second supporting observation to the sheep-dye proof of Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: Hair grows from the root, at the bottom.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The observation that dyed beards of old men turn white again, finished on the next amud.
